title: Six years an undertrial: the State pays

scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. An undertrial spends six years in jail, and is acquitted after a slipshod investigation. Can the Court make the State pay?
On twenty sixth October, twenty twenty six, Honourable Justice J B Pardiwala and Honourable Justice K Vinod Chandran of the Supreme Court ruled.
scenes.shown: On 26 October 2026, Honourable Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Honourable Justice K. Vinod Chandran of the Supreme Court ruled.

scenes.dialogue: The petitioner came to this Court for bail after six years in custody as an undertrial, in a case resting entirely on circumstantial evidence.
He was never named in the F I R or the Section One Sixty One statement. C C T V footage and a co-accused's confession made him an accused.
scenes.shown: He was never named in the FIR or the Section 161 statement. CCTV footage and a co-accused's confession made him an accused.

scenes.dialogue: In March twenty twenty six, this Court gave the trial court three months to finish the trial. That court then acquitted the petitioner, the only accused who faced trial.
scenes.shown: In March 2026, this Court gave the trial court three months to finish the trial. That court then acquitted the petitioner, the only accused who faced trial.

scenes.dialogue: None of four circumstances was proved: ransom claim, confessions, last seen, electronic evidence. Reading that judgment, the Court was appalled at the investigation.
The remains were not identified by D N A. The motorcycle was not produced. C C T V and call records had no Section Sixty Five B certificate.
scenes.shown: The remains were not identified by DNA. The motorcycle was not produced. CCTV and call records had no Section 65B certificate.

scenes.dialogue: Six years were erased from the life of a man, the Court said, on mere surmises and conjectures. The State Police would do well to educate their officers.
He was a victim of the system. The State must pay him six lakh rupees within one month, with eighteen per cent a year interest if late. The petition was disposed of.
scenes.shown: He was a victim of the system. The State must pay him ₹6 lakh within one month, with 18% a year interest if late. The petition was disposed of.
